components-actionbar.name: ActionBar
components-actionbar.description:
Use `ActionBar` to arrange actions in a horizontally scrolling row. Place `ActionButton` components inside it; their `visible` prop animates them in and out.

Set `wrap` to allow wrapping, or `disableShadow` to remove the overflow fades.

components-autocomplete.name: Autocomplete
components-autocomplete.description:
Use `Autocomplete.create<Item>()` for typed suggestions, or `Autocomplete.createGrouped<Group>()` for groups with an `items` array. Compose `Input`, `Content`, `List`, and `Item`, and use `value` and `onValueChange` to control the input text.

`Content` renders in a portal and accepts `arrow` and `positioner` options.

components-avatar.name: Avatar
components-avatar.description:
Pass `name` and optionally `imageSrc` to `Avatar`. It falls back to the first initial, or a profile icon when both are absent.

For overlapping avatars, use `AvatarList` with a `count` and an `index` on each `AvatarList.Item`.

components-box.name: Box
components-box.description:
`Box` is a flex layout wrapper: it defaults to a row, and `col` switches to a column. Use `gap`, `p`, `items`, `justify`, and `surface` for common layout and styling needs.

Use the `render` prop to render a different element while retaining the Box styles.

col.description: Apply flex-direction: column - default is row

layout.description: Apply both align-items and justify-content together

squish.description: Reduce padding in one axis by one level

emphasis.description: Overlaps with 'surface' - use surface as a boolean when provided.

m.description: Use margin to center self in flex

components-camera.name: Camera
components-camera.description:
`Camera` displays a live camera and sends a captured `File` to `onCapture`. Use `facingMode="environment"` to request a rear-facing camera.

Camera access requires browser permission and a secure context. `format` defaults to `image/png`, but photos taken with ImageCapture are not re-encoded to that format. Use `Camera.Root` and its controls for a custom layout.

components-checkbox.name: Checkbox
components-checkbox.description:
Use `Checkbox` with a label and, when controlled, `checked` and `onCheckedChange`. Set `checkedMode="faded"` to de-emphasize checked items, such as completed tasks.

For custom composition, use `Checkbox.Root` and `Checkbox.Indicator`.

checkedMode.description:
The checked visual state. Prominent mode means the checked version is visually
emphasized to the user. Faded means the checked version is visually de-emphasized.
Prominent is appropriate when the user's attention should be drawn to the 'on' state,
while faded is appropriate when a checked state means the item is 'done,' like in a task list.

stories.name: Default
stories.snippet: const Default = () => <Checkbox />;

components-chip.name: Chip
components-chip.description:
Use `Chip` for a compact label or piece of metadata. Choose `emphasis` to change its appearance.

For an interactive chip, use `render` with a semantic button or link so it is keyboard accessible.

components-collapsiblesimple.name: CollapsibleSimple
components-collapsiblesimple.description:
Compose `Collapsible` with `Collapsible.Trigger` and `Collapsible.Content`, or use `Collapsible.Simple` when the open state is managed elsewhere.

Content animates vertically by default; set `horizontal` or `both` for other directions.

stories.name: Default

components-colormodetoggle.name: ColorModeToggle
components-colormodetoggle.description:
`ColorModeToggle` offers system, light, and dark modes. By default it uses the shared color mode and persists explicit choices in local storage.

Pass `value` and `onValueChange` to manage the selection yourself; providing the callback replaces the default update.

stories.name: Default

components-combobox.name: Combobox
components-combobox.description:
Use `Combobox.create<Item>()` or `Combobox.createGrouped<Group>()` to select from typed items. Compose `Input`, `Content`, `List`, and `Item`; control selection with `value` and `onValueChange`.

The search text can be controlled separately with `inputValue` and `onInputValueChange`. Use `onCreate` and optionally `showCreatableItem` to offer new values.

stories.name: Default
Grouped
Not Popover

components-contextmenu.name: ContextMenu
components-contextmenu.description:
Wrap a target in `ContextMenu.Trigger` and put `ContextMenu.Item` elements inside `ContextMenu.Content`. Use `onSelect` on items to handle actions.

The menu opens from the context-menu gesture, renders in a portal, and stops click propagation from its content.

stories.name: Default

components-datepicker.name: DatePicker
components-datepicker.description:
`DatePicker` is controlled with a `Date | null` value and `onChange`. `DateRangePicker` uses the same pattern with `{ start, end }`, where each date may be null.

Both start by displaying the current month. Use their `Root` and calendar parts to customize the layout.

components-editabletext.name: EditableText
components-editabletext.description:
`EditableText` displays text that can be clicked to edit. Pass `value` and `onValueChange`; changes are reported as the user types.

Editing ends on Enter or blur. Pass `editing` and `onEditingChange` to control the editing state.

components-emojipicker.name: EmojiPicker
components-emojipicker.description:
Use `EmojiPicker` with `onValueChange`, which receives the emoji and its label. An optional `onClear` adds a clear action.

The prefab includes search and skin-tone controls; the skin-tone choice is stored in local storage. Use the exposed parts for a custom picker.

components-form.name: FormikForm
components-form.description:
`FormikForm` wraps Formik and a styled form. Provide `initialValues` and `onSubmit`, then use named fields such as `FormikForm.TextField`, `FormikForm.CheckboxField`, and `FormikForm.SubmitButton`. It also exposes `TextAreaField`, `NumberStepperField`, `SwitchField`, `ToggleGroupField`, and `EmojiField`.

Field names must match the Formik values. `Field` exposes `Label`, `Control`, `Description`, and `Error` for custom layouts.

stories.name: Default

components-horizontallist.description:
`HorizontalList` displays a scrolling row and can expand overflowing items into a wrapped layout. It manages its own open state, or accepts `open` and `onOpenChange`.

Use `onCanOpenChange` to observe whether content overflows and `disableInternalOpenToggle` to supply your own toggle.

components-imageuploader.name: ImageUploader
components-imageuploader.description:
`ImageUploader` takes an image URL or null as `value` and reports a `File | null` through `onChange`. It supports file selection, drag and drop, camera capture, and optional `altText`/`onAltText`.

`maxDimension` resizes selected or dropped files; camera captures bypass that resize. The caller is responsible for storing the file and updating the URL.

`Input` is a styled text input. Use `value` and `onValueChange` for a controlled value, and `startAccessory` or `endAccessory` for content inside its border.

`autoSelect` selects text on focus; `placeholders` can rotate placeholder text. Associate the input with a label, or use a form field.

components-layouts.name: PageRoot

`PageNav` hides while the keyboard is open. `PageNowPlaying` portals to the body by default; set `disablePortal` to keep it in place.

components-lightbox.name: Lightbox
components-lightbox.description:
Wrap a single element in `Lightbox` to use it as both the trigger and the enlarged content. `Lightbox.Image` provides image styling.

For different trigger and content elements, compose `Lightbox.Root`, `Trigger`, `Portal`, `Overlay`, and `Content` yourself.

stories.name: Default

components-lists.name: Ul
components-lists.description:
Use `Ol` or `Ul` with their `Item` parts for styled ordered or unordered lists. They render semantic list elements and accept normal list props.

Set `unstyled` to remove markers and default spacing.

stories.name: Ordered List
Unordered List
No Markers

components-liveupdatetextfield.name: LiveUpdateTextField
components-liveupdatetextfield.description:
Use `LiveUpdateTextField` with `value` and `onChange` for optimistic, debounced updates. The default debounce is 500ms; set `debounceMs` to change it, or `textArea` for multiline input.

External value changes are ignored while focused. Blur sends an edited value immediately, even if a debounced update was already sent.

reactDocgen.description:
An extension of TextField which keeps a local realtime value in state and
periodically reports changes to the parent. Use this to connect
to the API and update a value from the field directly.

This component is optimistic and will not respond to external changes while focused.

stories.name: Default

components-marquee.name: Marquee
components-marquee.description: Place `Marquee.Item` children inside `Marquee` to cycle through them one at a time. The `timeout` prop controls the interval in milliseconds and defaults to 5000.

stories.name: Default

components-masonry.name: Masonry
components-masonry.description:
`Masonry` arranges its direct children into columns based on their measured heights. Set `columns` to a number or a function of container width, and `gap` to a pixel value.

Set `data-span` on a child, or spread `masonrySpan(n)`, to span multiple columns.

stories.name: Default
With Span

components-note.name: Note
components-note.description:
`Note` renders its children in a folded-note surface. Use `Note.Input` for an editable, auto-sizing text area inside it.

`Note.Input` is the input itself rather than a complete labeled field, so provide a label when editing.

stories.name: Default
stories.snippet: const Default = () => <Note>This is a note</Note>;

stories.name: Editable

components-numberstepper.name: NumberStepper
components-numberstepper.description:
`NumberStepper` is controlled with a numeric `value` and `onChange`. Use `increment` for a fixed step or `steps` for a list of allowed values; the current value should be in that list.

`min` and `max` disable buttons at the boundaries but do not clamp a step that crosses them.

stories.name: Default
stories.snippet: const Default = () => <NumberStepper value={0} />;

components-particlelayer.name: ParticleLayer
components-particlelayer.description:
`ParticleLayer` provides a canvas and particle state to descendants; use `useParticles()` to create effects. `Provider` already includes a layer unless `disableParticles` is set.

The canvas is portaled to the body by default; `noPortal` keeps it in place. The layer and its children render after the client mounts, not during server rendering.

stories.name: Default
Hidden Test

components-particlelayer.import: import { Button, Checkbox, Icon, ParticleLayer } from '@a-type/ui';

components-peek.name: Peek
components-peek.description: `Peek` initially shows a limited height of its children and provides a toggle when the content overflows. Set `peekHeight` in pixels; it defaults to 120. The expanded state is managed internally.

components-popover.name: Popover
components-popover.description:
Compose `Popover` with `Popover.Trigger` and `Popover.Content`; add `Title`, `Description`, and `Close` as appropriate. The trigger can render a custom button through `render`.

Content is portaled and accepts positioning props such as `side` and `align`. Add `Popover.Arrow` explicitly if desired.

stories.name: Default

components-progress.name: Progress
components-progress.description:
Pass `value` and optionally `max` to `Progress` to show completion; `max` defaults to 100. Use `Progress.Labeled` with a `label` for a visible label and value.

The `Root`, `Track`, `Indicator`, `Label`, and `Value` parts are available for custom composition.

stories.name: Default
Labeled

components-pwainstalltrigger.name: PwaInstallTrigger
components-pwainstalltrigger.description:
`PwaInstallTrigger` opens the install dialog supplied by `Provider` and hides when the app is already installed. It renders an Install button by default and accepts custom children.

The provider loads `/manifest.json` by default; use `manifestPath` to change it. Setting `manifestPath={false}` removes the install dialog, so the trigger will not open one.

stories.name: Default

components-quickaction.name: QuickAction
components-quickaction.description:
Compose `QuickAction` with `QuickAction.Trigger` and `QuickAction.Content` for an action panel anchored to its trigger. Set `align` on the content to `start`, `center`, or `end`.

The popup is portaled and uses CSS anchor positioning, so positioning depends on browser support.

stories.name: Default
stories.snippet:
const Default = args => {
    return (
        <PageRoot>
            <PageContent>
                <PageNowPlaying
                    className={clsx({
                        'items-center': args.align === 'center',
                        'items-start': args.align === 'start',
                        'items-end': args.align === 'end',
                    })}
                    style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column' }}>
                    <QuickAction>
                        <QuickAction.Trigger>
                            <Icon name="plus" />
                        </QuickAction.Trigger>
                        <QuickAction.Content style={{ width: '95vw' }} align={args.align}>
                            <ActionContent />
                        </QuickAction.Content>
                    </QuickAction>
                </PageNowPlaying>
            </PageContent>
            <PageNav>
                <NavBar>
                    <NavBarItem>
                        <NavBarItemIcon name="home" />
                        <NavBarItemText>Home</NavBarItemText>
                    </NavBarItem>
                </NavBar>
            </PageNav>
        </PageRoot>
    );
};

components-relativetime.name: RelativeTime
components-relativetime.description:
Pass a timestamp in milliseconds as `value` to display a relative time. Use `abbreviate` for shorter units or `disableRelativeText` to omit "ago" and "from now".

The text updates every minute; `countdownSeconds` updates once per second for future times less than a minute away.

countdownSeconds.description:
Makes it count down seconds for a future date value as it approaches.
Does not affect past dates.

disableRelativeText.description: Remove "from now" or "ago" from the output.

stories.name: Default
stories.snippet: const Default = () => <RelativeTime value={Date.now() + 60 * 1000 * 2} abbreviate={false} />;

components-scrollarea.name: ScrollArea
components-scrollarea.description:
Give `ScrollArea` a constrained size and choose `direction` (`vertical`, `horizontal`, or `both`). Put the scrollable children in `ScrollArea.Content`.

Fades are included by default; set `disableFades` to remove them. Use `Root`, `Viewport`, and `Scrollbar` for a custom composition.

components-select.name: Select
components-select.description:
Compose `Select` with `Select.Trigger`, `Select.Content`, and `Select.Item` elements. Use `value` and `onValueChange` for a controlled selection, or `defaultValue` for an initial value.

The trigger displays the selected value and a chevron by default. Use `itemToStringLabel` when values need a custom display label.

Compare Select And Button

components-textskeleton.name: TextSkeleton
components-textskeleton.description:
Use `TextSkeleton` as a placeholder for text while content loads. Pass `maxLength` to influence its randomly chosen width, which stays fixed for that mount.

Provide loading status separately for assistive technology.

stories.name: Default
On Background

components-slider.name: Slider
components-slider.description:
Use `Slider` with `defaultValue`, or control it with `value` and `onValueChange`; configure `min`, `max`, and `step` as needed. `Slider.getSingle` extracts one value from a number or value array.

For a labeled thumb or a displayed value, compose `Slider.Root`, `Slider.Ui`, and `Slider.Value`.

stories.snippet: const Default = () => <Slider />;

    <Slider.Value />

components-spinner.name: Spinner
components-spinner.description:
Use `Spinner` to indicate ongoing work and provide an accessible label such as `aria-label="Loading"`. `size` is in pixels and defaults to 40; pass `null` to size it with CSS.

`FullScreenSpinner` centers a spinner while filling the available flex space.

stories.snippet: const Default = () => <Spinner />;

stories.snippet: const Small = () => <Spinner size={20} thickness={4} />;

stories.name: Large
stories.snippet: const Large = () => <Spinner size={80} thickness={12} />;

components-splashscreen.name: SplashScreen
components-splashscreen.description: Use `SplashScreen` as a startup surface that fills its container, and place an image or logo inside `SplashScreen.Icon`. Both parts accept `render` when a different underlying element is needed.

stories.name: Default

components-switch.name: Switch
components-switch.description:
Use `Switch` for an on/off setting, with an associated label. Control it with `checked` and `onCheckedChange`, or provide `defaultChecked`.

The default includes a thumb; use `Switch.Root` and `Switch.Thumb` for custom composition.

stories.name: Default

components-tabs.name: Tabs
components-tabs.description:
Compose `Tabs` with `Tabs.List`, `Tabs.Trigger`, and matching `Tabs.Content` values. Use `value` and `onValueChange` to control the active tab.

The tab list scrolls horizontally when its triggers do not fit.

stories.name: Default
With Many Tabs

components-tabs.import: import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsRoot, TabsTrigger } from '@a-type/ui';

components-textarea.name: TextArea
components-textarea.description:
`TextArea` is a multiline input with the same `onValueChange` and placeholder options as `Input`. It auto-sizes by default; set `autoSize={false}` to use a fixed number of `rows`.

Use `TextArea.Border` and `TextArea.Input` for custom composition, and provide an associated label.

components-toasts.name: Toaster
components-toasts.description:
Call `toast`, `toast.success`, or `toast.error` to show a message. `toast.promise` tracks a promise, and `toast.loading` returns a `complete` function for a later update.

`Provider` mounts the toast provider and `Toaster`. Use `timeout` in milliseconds and `data.actions` for optional actions.

stories.name: Default

components-togglegroup.name: ToggleGroup
components-togglegroup.description:
Use `ToggleGroup` with `ToggleGroup.Item` children, each with a `value`. The controlled `value` and `onValueChange` use an array, even for single selection.

Set `multiple` to allow more than one item to be selected.

reactDocgen.description:
Provides a shared state to a series of toggle buttons.

Documentation: [Base UI Toggle Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toggle-group)

stories.name: Default

components-tooltip.name: Tooltip
components-tooltip.description:
Wrap one trigger element in `Tooltip` and provide its `content`. Use `side`, `sideOffset`, or `color` to adjust the popup, and `disabled` to bypass the tooltip.

Tooltips need a `TooltipProvider`; the library `Provider` already supplies one.

stories.name: Default
Disabled
Color
Customized

components-typography.name: Text
components-typography.description:
Use `Text`, `Heading`, `HeroText`, `P`, and `TextLink` for styled typography. Props such as `emphasis`, `bold`, `dim`, and `truncate` adjust presentation.

`Heading` renders a span by default: use `render={<h2 />}` (or another heading level) for semantic headings. The `H1` through `H5` helpers are deprecated.

components-viewport.name: Viewport
components-viewport.description:
`Viewport` provides pan and zoom for its children. Give it a constrained size and add `Viewport.Control` with `Viewport.ZoomControls` for visible controls.

Configure `minZoom`, `maxZoom`, and the default center or zoom as needed. Use `viewportRef` outside the viewport or `useViewport()` in a descendant for programmatic control.

viewportRef.description: Get access to the viewport from outside this component
